title: Prognostic load-shedding + silent handoff playbook for SLO-safe multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: transient spikes and slow tails in the serving runtime periodically produce high-volume low-severity alerts that lead to premature region failovers, noisy pages, and expensive full-failover churn. Current circuit breakers are binary and trigger broad route evacuation rather than a graded graceful degrade. On-call teams lack a concise silent-handoff/runbook pattern that allows the platform to autonomously shed load and route higher-quality traffic while preserving SLOs for critical customers.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive load-shedding signals computed and emitted to routing layer with <500ms decision latency under 95th percentile request load
Silent handoff sequence implemented: notify oncall with non-paging severity, begin graded shedding, activate soft circuit-breaker rules, then escalate only if SLOs still degrade
Runbook automation triggers an instrumented canary failover (region drain) only after prognostic signal persists beyond configured hysteresis
End-to-end test suite verifying no more than 10% increase in p99 latency for critical routes during controlled shedding experiments
Dashboards and alert thresholds added; oncall sees reduced noise (target >40% fewer P1 pages for transient events) after rollout
implementation_notes: Create a new prognostic signal pipeline: aggregate short-window latency histograms, token-queue depth, gRPC IO stalls, and KV-cache miss-rate into an ML-lite scoring function (threshold and trend outputs)
Extend routing layer to accept graded decisions: PASS, THROTTLE-LOW, THROTTLE-CRITICAL, SOFT-REJECT. Map request classes by route tags (critical, best-effort, background)
Introduce 'soft-stop' circuit-breaker that marks backends as degraded without triggering global evacuations; backpressure informs autoscaler but does not immediate failover
Build an oncall silent-handoff workflow: non-paging alert with detailed context, automated remediation attempt (redispatch, spinner cache warming), and automated re-eval windows before escalation
Add idempotent automation hooks to runbook that can be executed by playbook agent and by human oncall equally
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy prognostic scoring + soft-breaker to a single EU region (10% traffic) for non-critical test tenants. Validate decision latency and false-positive rate over 72 hours
Phase 2 (Regional Expand): Expand to NA-east for background routes, monitor MP (missed pages) and customer error budget consumption for 7 days
Phase 3 (Tiered Rollout): Enable for critical routes with conservative thresholds and longer hysteresis; enable silent-handoff notifications to oncall but keep paging off
Phase 4 (Full): Flip default for best-effort routes across regions. Monitor for unintended full-failovers and rollback thresholds defined below
rollback_plan: Immediate: Revert routing decision ingestion to previous stable branch (toggle feature flag). This stops graded shedding within 30s for all regions
If revert fails: Disable prognostic scoring by shutting the scoring service replica set; routing will fall back to current static heuristics
Post-rollback: Run root-cause diagnostics on false-positive triggers and adjust thresholds/hysteresis before next attempt
test_plan: Synthetic tail-latency injection using chaos harness to create short bursts and verify that prognostic signal suppresses paging for transient events
Load tests across traffic mixes to measure decision latency (<500ms) and overall p95/p99 impact per route class
End-to-end blue/green test validating silent-handoff notifications, automated remediation attempts, and escalation path when automated remediation fails
Purple-team test where oncall practices silent handoff steps in staging and validates automation idempotency
Regression test: Ensure no customer sessions are dropped for critical routes when soft-breaker engages
monitoring_dashboards: SLO fusion dashboard: request success rate, user-visible latency, regional error budget burn broken down by route class
Prognostic signal health: score distribution, precision/recall on labeled incidents, decision latency histogram
Soft-breaker state: counts by state, time-in-state, backpressure signals to autoscaler
Oncall noise metric: P1/P2 page counts pre/post rollout, grouped by cause (transient latency, backend error, infra)
Failover-safety checks: number of automated canary evacuations, number of human-triggered failovers, and mean time between unnecessary failovers
